## Developer Guide

If you are new to using `nbdev` here are some useful pointers to get you started.

### Install pymlx90642 in Development mode

```sh
# make sure pymlx90642 package is installed in development mode
$ pip install -e .

# make changes under nbs/ directory
# ...

# compile to have changes apply to pymlx90642
$ nbdev_prepare
```

## Usage

### Installation

Install latest from the GitHub [repository][repo]:

```sh
$ pip install git+https://github.com/ecamo19/pymlx90642.git
```

or from [conda][conda]

```sh
$ conda install -c ecamo19 pymlx90642
```

or from [pypi][pypi]


```sh
$ pip install pymlx90642
```

## How to use

## Configure raspberry pi:

::: {#cell-14 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Update system
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

# Install Python packages
sudo apt install i2c-tools -y
```
:::


::: {#cell-15 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Enable I2C interface
sudo raspi-config

# Navigate to: Interface Options > I2C > Yes

# Reboot
sudo reboot

# Verify I2C is working
sudo i2cdetect -y 1


# You should see device at address 0x33 (default MLX90642 address)

#| hide
```
